doc.tool: Read the dual-Franka runtime conventions, camera aliases, VLA policy conditioning text, semantic stop rules, and available primitive names before acting. This is read-only.
Read a dual-Franka state snapshot. Configured inline camera views are returned directly; other available views are returned as artifact paths; use read to inspect these artifacts.
Read camera intrinsics, serials, and projection metadata for the dual-Franka rig.

camera.description: Registered projection view name, e.g. d455 or base (default d455). Valid names come from perception.projection_views and the current state's saved artifacts.

doc.tool: Back-project one pixel from a registered RGBD camera view into shared right-base coordinates. Use a camera listed by view_env_state/view_camera_meta; default is the configured primary metric localization camera.

camera.description: Registered projection view name, e.g. d455 or base (default d455). Valid names come from perception.projection_views and the current state's saved artifacts.

prompt.description: Text prompt for SAM3. Prefer short object/relation phrases; for the clean-desk box use 'white interior of the black cardboard box' or 'cardboard box'. Avoid over-specific surface words such as 'floor' when grounding is weak. Provide exactly one of prompt or point.

point.description: Positive SAM3 point in camera image coordinates [row, col]. Provide exactly one of prompt or point.

doc.tool: Use SAM3 on a registered RGB image with either a text prompt or one positive [row, col] point, return a mask overlay for verification, and estimate the mask median point in shared right-base coordinates.

doc.code:
Both arms' state: TCP poses (right_base, xyz + quaternion xyzw), joints and gripper widths.

Example:
    st = get_robot_state()
    print(st["left_arm"]["tcp_pose"][:3], st["right_arm"]["tcp_pose"][:3])

Live RGB-D frames of the rig's cameras.

Example:
    obs = get_observation()
    print(sorted(k for k in obs if k.endswith("_images")))

Camera intrinsics, serials and projection metadata.

Example:
    meta = get_camera_meta()
    print(meta["observation_camera_map"])

xyz.description: TCP position, right_base [x, y, z] in m

doc.code:
IK reach check of one arm's TCP pose (right_base) from its current joints, nothing moves (--ik): {status: reachable | unreachable | unknown, q, message}.

Example:
    print(preview_reach([0.4, 0.2, 0.2], arm="left")["status"])

arm.description: Which arm to command; the other arm is left uncommanded.

doc.tool: Move one Franka TCP by a bounded world-frame (right_base) xyz delta in meters (at most {{max_move}} m per call; refused when it ends outside the workspace or below the z floor).
doc.code:
Translate one arm's TCP by a right_base delta in metres; refused beyond the per-call limit (--max-move) or outside the workspace (--workspace-xy, --z-floor).

Example:
    move_delta("left", [0, 0, 0.03])  # the left TCP 3 cm up

arm.description: Which arm to command; the other arm is left uncommanded.

doc.tool: Rotate one Franka TCP by a bounded world-frame (right_base) rpy delta in radians (at most {{max_rotate}} rad per call, norm of delta_rpy).
doc.code:
Rotate one arm's TCP by a right_base roll/pitch/yaw delta in radians; refused beyond the per-call limit (--max-rotate).

Example:
    rotate_delta("right", [0, 0, -0.2])

arm.description: Which arm to command; the other arm is left uncommanded.

doc.code:
Open (open=True) or close one arm's gripper and wait for it to settle.

Example:
    set_gripper("right", True)  # open

arm.description: Which arm to command; the other arm is left uncommanded.

doc.tool: Open one Franka gripper and wait for the command to settle.
doc.code:
Open one arm's gripper fully and wait for it to settle (CaP-X's open_gripper, per arm).

Example:
    open_gripper("left")

arm.description: Which arm to command; the other arm is left uncommanded.

doc.tool: Close one Franka gripper and wait for the command to settle.
doc.code:
Close one arm's gripper and wait for it to settle (CaP-X's close_gripper, per arm).

Example:
    close_gripper("right")

doc.tool: Reset both arms to their healthy configured joint posture while preserving each gripper's open/closed state. Closed grippers are re-commanded before/after the joint reset so held objects stay clamped, then both TCPs return near their prior poses.

prompt.description: Planner-facing segment intent. This is recorded in the tool result; the current live clean-desk checkpoint still receives its fixed training instruction during policy inference.

doc.tool: Run the learned right-grasp VLA segment. The active task prompt decides which object is currently allowed; this tool only defines the capability boundary: right gripper closes and the right TCP lifts.

prompt.description: Planner-facing segment intent. This is recorded in the tool result; the current live clean-desk checkpoint still receives its fixed training instruction during policy inference.

doc.tool: Run the learned bimanual handoff VLA segment. The capability boundary is right-gripper release followed by the configured settle delay; do not rule-base pre-position either arm for it.

prompt.description: Planner-facing segment intent. This is recorded in the tool result; the current live clean-desk checkpoint still receives its fixed training instruction during policy inference.

doc.tool: Run the learned left-placement VLA segment. The active task decides the destination; this tool only defines the capability boundary: left gripper opens and the left TCP lifts.

object.description: Object to grasp (SAM3 text prompt), e.g. 'black bowl'

mask_id.description: A mask id (d2) of the current observation instead of object

camera.description: Registered RGB-D view name (default: the first configured)

arm.description: Which arm to command; the other arm is left uncommanded.

next_after.description: Greedy policy: reject this grasp id and return the next rank of its plan

reason.description: With next_after: why that candidate failed

region.description: The surface it goes onto / into (SAM3 text), or region_mask_id

region_mask_id.description: Mask id of the placement region

grasp_id.description: A current grasp (g id) of this observation, the one the object will be held with

object_mask_id.description: The object's mask id; default the mask the grasp was planned on

camera.description: Registered RGB-D view name (default: the first configured)

object.description: The object that should be in the gripper

arm.description: Which arm to command; the other arm is left uncommanded.
